inputs.name: kappa
inputs.cite: PR-1 (paul@L46): '1 mutation for every 10 billion bases'

inputs.name: hours_per_year
inputs.cite: Julian year; 365 d gives the same rounded figures

day.reading: the model saturates bacteria within 100 My, which no real genome shows; what stops real genomes saturating is constraint and fixation dynamics the model leaves out
day.holds: D/L = 10.8% at 1 My, 59.2% at 10 My, 75.0% at 100 My; 'the maximum' is the expected saturation value, not the possible maximum (1.0)

critic.reading: Paul's point is that copying errors alone produce too much divergence, not too little; the figure illustrates supply, not a prediction for real bacteria
critic.holds: the numbers reproduce; at L = 4.6e6 the realised fraction sits within 0.0002 (one SD) of 0.75, so '75% is the maximum' is a practical ceiling and a wording slip only

notes: Every bacteria number in the EVOA-102 review reproduces from Paul's inputs (59.2% is the review's '59%'). The 30-min figure (74.3% at 1 My) is superseded by Paul's own CORRECTION (rule SC). 'This is still way faster than any evolutionary model would predict' has no model named; neutral models at unconstrained sites also saturate over 100 My at these inputs.
